pr_body:
`fileDetails` is accessed via `synchronized` lock on the Index object, but is published without one and it's not immutable, so it can be seen in incomplete state outside of the thread where it was constructed. 

Fixes #87568

review_comments:
I am not sure this is necessary. Here, `fileDetails` is a final field that is initialized here in `Index` constructor.

According to the https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se7/html/jls-17.html#jls-17.5
`An object is considered to be completely initialized when its constructor finishes. A thread that can only see a reference to an object after that object has been completely initialized is guaranteed to see the correctly initialized values for that object's final fields.`

My understanding is that (event though `fileDetails` itself is mutable) it will be completely initialized (read from `in` in this case) by the time another thread can have a chance to see it and lock for other updates or reads. Do I miss anything?
You're right. I think we don't synchronized on this because `fileDetails` is final, so there's a read barrier that guarantees safe initialization
